roleTitle: Operations Process Specialist, Collaboration Software Subscriptions
jobDescription: The subscription operations team of a collaboration-software vendor handles seat changes, renewals and billing corrections for business customers. The Operations Process Specialist owns the renewal-processing procedure, maintains the billing-correction checklist, coordinates with finance and customer success on disputed invoices, and is expected to lower the share of renewals that need manual correction, reported against the team's quarterly baseline.
requirements: Runs the renewal-processing procedure for business subscriptions in the billing system.
Maintains the billing-correction checklist and the list of known correction causes.
Lowers the share of renewals needing manual correction, reported against the quarterly baseline.
Coordinates disputed invoices with finance and customer success and records own responsibility boundaries.
Documents known limitations and hand-over conditions at each quarter-end.

evidence.text: Processed monthly and annual renewals for business subscriptions in the billing system, checking seat counts against the customer's admin console export before each invoice run.

Maintained the billing-correction checklist and the running list of correction causes (seat-count drift, expired purchase orders, currency mismatch), adding a pre-invoice seat check after a wave of seat-count corrections.
Handled disputed invoices with finance and customer success through the dispute queue; credit notes above the agreed limit were approved by the finance controller.
Prepared the quarter-end hand-over note for the subscription operations lead, listing open disputes, corrections in progress and the causes still unresolved.
Responsibilities included renewal processing, checklist maintenance, dispute handling and quarter-end hand-over for the subscription operations team over roughly two years.
Work sample: the billing-correction checklist with the pre-invoice seat check and the correction-cause list for one quarter, with the billing system's case numbers as a verification trail.
Candidate's cover email: 'After I introduced the pre-invoice seat check, manual corrections dropped from about one in five renewals to almost none.' No report or figure source was attached.

Hiring manager pre-read: the finance controller wants the correction rate down this year and has asked for evidence that the candidate has moved that number before; please separate what is documented from what is claimed.

propositions.text: The candidate processed business subscription renewals in the billing system, checking seat counts against the admin console export before each invoice run.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the renewal processing and the seat check directly.

propositions.text: The candidate maintained the billing-correction checklist and the correction-cause list and added a pre-invoice seat check.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the checklist work sample document the maintenance and the added step.

propositions.text: The candidate's pre-invoice seat check reduced manual corrections from one in five renewals to almost none.
propositions.rationale: The figure appears only in the candidate's own cover email without a report, baseline or period.

gold.expectedGap: No report, baseline or period in the materials measures the share of renewals needing manual correction before and after the seat check.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Treat the cover-email figure as the candidate's own claim; the materials document the checklist change, not the change in correction rate.
followUpTargets: Ask for the quarterly correction-rate report or the billing-system extract that shows corrections before and after the seat check was introduced.
